facts.statement: Gobiosuchus lived during the Early Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous in the Bayn Dzak locality of the Djadochta Formation in the Gobi Desert of Mongolia.
facts.quote: It hails from the Late Cretaceous (Early Campanian) of Bayn Dzak (Djadokhta Formation), in the Gobi Desert of Mongolia.

facts.statement: The type species Gobiosuchus kielanae is classified within the family Gobiosuchidae.
facts.quote: The type species is Gobiosuchus kielanae, classified as a member of the family Gobiosuchidae.

facts.statement: Gobiosuchus was a small, gracile animal featuring long, slender limbs and a relatively elongated neck.
facts.quote: Gobiosuchus is a small and gracile animal with long, slender limbs (despite the comparatively small pectoral and pelvic girdles) and a relatively elongated neck.

facts.statement: Gobiosuchus possessed heavy armor consisting of overlapping cylindrical rings of dermal scutes around the neck, torso, and tail, with 8 transverse rows on the neck and 10 on the torso.
facts.quote: It is very heavily armoured, with several transverse rows of dorsal and ventral osteoderms that correspond to each vertebra and meet laterally, forming overlapping cylindrical "rings" of dermal scutes surrounding the entirety of the neck (8 transverse rows), torso (10 transverse rows), and tail.

facts.statement: Thickened ridges on the posterior end of the cervical and thoracic scutes limited the animal's flexibility despite its elongated body proportions.
facts.quote: The cervical and thoracic scutes have a thickened ridge on their posterior end, where they overlapped the next ring behind it, limiting flexibility despite the elongated proportions.

facts.statement: The palate contained pits for sharp, conical teeth, with the largest pit accommodating an enlarged fourth dentary tooth.
facts.quote: The palate possesses several pits to receive the sharp, conical teeth of the lower jaw, with the biggest of these corresponding to the enlarged fourth dentary tooth.

facts.statement: Gobiosuchus kielanae forms the family Gobiosuchidae together with Zaraasuchus shepardi.
facts.quote: Gobiosuchus kielanae, junto con Zaraasuchus shepardi forma la familia Gobiosuchidae

facts.statement: The time range for Gobiosuchus is the Campanian stage, spanning from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

rejected.quote: Gobiosuchus is an extinct genus of crocodyliform described in 1972 by Polish palaeontologist Halszka Osmólska.
